scene.label: Act 4, Scene 2
scene.title: SCENE II. Before the Duke of Albany's Palace
scene.location: Before the Duke of Albany's Palace

content.text: Enter Goneril, Edmund; Oswald meeting them.

lines.text: Welcome, my lord. I marvel our mild husband
lines.plainText: Welcome my lord I marvel our mild husband

lines.text: Not met us on the way. Now, where's your master?
lines.plainText: Not met us on the way Now where's your master

lines.text: Madam, within; but never man so chang'd.
lines.plainText: Madam within but never man so chang'd

lines.text: I told him of the army that was landed;
lines.plainText: I told him of the army that was landed

lines.text: He smil'd at it: I told him you were coming;
lines.plainText: He smil'd at it I told him you were coming

lines.text: His answer was, 'The worse.' Of Gloucester's treachery
lines.plainText: His answer was 'The worse' Of Gloucester's treachery

lines.text: And of the loyal service of his son
lines.plainText: And of the loyal service of his son

lines.text: When I inform'd him, then he call'd me sot,
lines.plainText: When I inform'd him then he call'd me sot

lines.text: And told me I had turn'd the wrong side out.
lines.plainText: And told me I had turn'd the wrong side out

lines.text: What most he should dislike seems pleasant to him;
lines.plainText: What most he should dislike seems pleasant to him

lines.text: What like, offensive.
lines.plainText: What like offensive

lines.text: [To Edmund.] Then shall you go no further.
lines.plainText: To Edmund Then shall you go no further

lines.text: It is the cowish terror of his spirit,
lines.plainText: It is the cowish terror of his spirit

lines.text: That dares not undertake. He'll not feel wrongs
lines.plainText: That dares not undertake He'll not feel wrongs

lines.text: Which tie him to an answer. Our wishes on the way
lines.plainText: Which tie him to an answer Our wishes on the way

lines.text: May prove effects. Back, Edmund, to my brother;
lines.plainText: May prove effects Back Edmund to my brother

lines.text: Hasten his musters and conduct his powers.
lines.plainText: Hasten his musters and conduct his powers

lines.text: I must change names at home, and give the distaff
lines.plainText: I must change names at home and give the distaff

lines.text: Into my husband's hands. This trusty servant
lines.plainText: Into my husband's hands This trusty servant

lines.text: Shall pass between us. Ere long you are like to hear,
lines.plainText: Shall pass between us Ere long you are like to hear

lines.text: If you dare venture in your own behalf,
lines.plainText: If you dare venture in your own behalf

lines.text: A mistress's command. [Giving a favour.]
lines.plainText: A mistress's command Giving a favour

lines.text: Wear this; spare speech;
lines.plainText: Wear this spare speech

lines.text: Decline your head. This kiss, if it durst speak,
lines.plainText: Decline your head This kiss if it durst speak

lines.text: Would stretch thy spirits up into the air.
lines.plainText: Would stretch thy spirits up into the air

lines.text: Conceive, and fare thee well.
lines.plainText: Conceive and fare thee well

lines.text: Yours in the ranks of death.
lines.plainText: Yours in the ranks of death

lines.text: My most dear Gloucester.
lines.plainText: My most dear Gloucester

lines.text: O, the difference of man and man!
lines.plainText: O the difference of man and man

lines.text: To thee a woman's services are due;
lines.plainText: To thee a woman's services are due

lines.text: My fool usurps my body.
lines.plainText: My fool usurps my body

lines.text: Madam, here comes my lord.
lines.plainText: Madam here comes my lord

lines.text: I have been worth the whistle.
lines.plainText: I have been worth the whistle

lines.text: O Goneril!
lines.plainText: O Goneril

lines.text: You are not worth the dust which the rude wind
lines.plainText: You are not worth the dust which the rude wind

lines.text: Blows in your face! I fear your disposition;
lines.plainText: Blows in your face I fear your disposition

lines.text: That nature which contemns its origin
lines.plainText: That nature which contemns its origin

lines.text: Cannot be bordered certain in itself.
lines.plainText: Cannot be bordered certain in itself

lines.text: She that herself will sliver and disbranch
lines.plainText: She that herself will sliver and disbranch

lines.text: From her material sap, perforce must wither
lines.plainText: From her material sap perforce must wither

lines.text: And come to deadly use.
lines.plainText: And come to deadly use

lines.text: No more; the text is foolish.
lines.plainText: No more the text is foolish

lines.text: Wisdom and goodness to the vile seem vile;
lines.plainText: Wisdom and goodness to the vile seem vile

lines.text: Filths savour but themselves. What have you done?
lines.plainText: Filths savour but themselves What have you done

lines.text: Tigers, not daughters, what have you perform'd?
lines.plainText: Tigers not daughters what have you perform'd

lines.text: A father, and a gracious aged man,
lines.plainText: A father and a gracious aged man

lines.text: Whose reverence even the head-lugg'd bear would lick,
lines.plainText: Whose reverence even the headlugg'd bear would lick

lines.text: Most barbarous, most degenerate, have you madded.
lines.plainText: Most barbarous most degenerate have you madded

lines.text: Could my good brother suffer you to do it?
lines.plainText: Could my good brother suffer you to do it

lines.text: A man, a prince, by him so benefitted!
lines.plainText: A man a prince by him so benefitted

lines.text: If that the heavens do not their visible spirits
lines.plainText: If that the heavens do not their visible spirits

lines.text: Send quickly down to tame these vile offences,
lines.plainText: Send quickly down to tame these vile offences

lines.text: It will come,
lines.plainText: It will come

lines.text: Humanity must perforce prey on itself,
lines.plainText: Humanity must perforce prey on itself

lines.text: Like monsters of the deep.
lines.plainText: Like monsters of the deep

lines.text: Milk-liver'd man!
lines.plainText: Milkliver'd man

lines.text: That bear'st a cheek for blows, a head for wrongs;
lines.plainText: That bear'st a cheek for blows a head for wrongs

lines.text: Who hast not in thy brows an eye discerning
lines.plainText: Who hast not in thy brows an eye discerning

lines.text: Thine honour from thy suffering; that not know'st
lines.plainText: Thine honour from thy suffering that not know'st

lines.text: Fools do those villains pity who are punish'd
lines.plainText: Fools do those villains pity who are punish'd

lines.text: Ere they have done their mischief. Where's thy drum?
lines.plainText: Ere they have done their mischief Where's thy drum

lines.text: France spreads his banners in our noiseless land;
lines.plainText: France spreads his banners in our noiseless land

lines.text: With plumed helm thy state begins to threat,
lines.plainText: With plumed helm thy state begins to threat

lines.text: Whilst thou, a moral fool, sitt'st still, and criest
lines.plainText: Whilst thou a moral fool sitt'st still and criest

lines.text: 'Alack, why does he so?'
lines.plainText: 'Alack why does he so'

lines.text: See thyself, devil!
lines.plainText: See thyself devil

lines.text: Proper deformity seems not in the fiend
lines.plainText: Proper deformity seems not in the fiend

lines.text: So horrid as in woman.
lines.plainText: So horrid as in woman

lines.text: O vain fool!
lines.plainText: O vain fool

lines.text: Thou changed and self-cover'd thing, for shame!
lines.plainText: Thou changed and selfcover'd thing for shame

lines.text: Be-monster not thy feature! Were't my fitness
lines.plainText: Bemonster not thy feature Were't my fitness

lines.text: To let these hands obey my blood,
lines.plainText: To let these hands obey my blood

lines.text: They are apt enough to dislocate and tear
lines.plainText: They are apt enough to dislocate and tear

lines.text: Thy flesh and bones. Howe'er thou art a fiend,
lines.plainText: Thy flesh and bones Howe'er thou art a fiend

lines.text: A woman's shape doth shield thee.
lines.plainText: A woman's shape doth shield thee

lines.text: Marry, your manhood, mew!
lines.plainText: Marry your manhood mew

lines.text: What news?
lines.plainText: What news

lines.text: O, my good lord, the Duke of Cornwall's dead;
lines.plainText: O my good lord the Duke of Cornwall's dead

lines.text: Slain by his servant, going to put out
lines.plainText: Slain by his servant going to put out

lines.text: The other eye of Gloucester.
lines.plainText: The other eye of Gloucester

lines.text: Gloucester's eyes!
lines.plainText: Gloucester's eyes

lines.text: A servant that he bred, thrill'd with remorse,
lines.plainText: A servant that he bred thrill'd with remorse

lines.text: Oppos'd against the act, bending his sword
lines.plainText: Oppos'd against the act bending his sword

lines.text: To his great master; who, thereat enrag'd,
lines.plainText: To his great master who thereat enrag'd

lines.text: Flew on him, and amongst them fell'd him dead;
lines.plainText: Flew on him and amongst them fell'd him dead

lines.text: But not without that harmful stroke which since
lines.plainText: But not without that harmful stroke which since

lines.text: Hath pluck'd him after.
lines.plainText: Hath pluck'd him after

lines.text: This shows you are above,
lines.plainText: This shows you are above

lines.text: You justicers, that these our nether crimes
lines.plainText: You justicers that these our nether crimes

lines.text: So speedily can venge! But, O poor Gloucester!
lines.plainText: So speedily can venge But O poor Gloucester

lines.text: Lost he his other eye?
lines.plainText: Lost he his other eye

lines.text: Both, both, my lord.
lines.plainText: Both both my lord

lines.text: This letter, madam, craves a speedy answer;
lines.plainText: This letter madam craves a speedy answer

lines.text: 'Tis from your sister.
lines.plainText: 'Tis from your sister

lines.text: [Aside.] One way I like this well;
lines.plainText: Aside One way I like this well

lines.text: But being widow, and my Gloucester with her,
lines.plainText: But being widow and my Gloucester with her

lines.text: May all the building in my fancy pluck
lines.plainText: May all the building in my fancy pluck

lines.text: Upon my hateful life. Another way
lines.plainText: Upon my hateful life Another way

lines.text: The news is not so tart. I'll read, and answer.
lines.plainText: The news is not so tart I'll read and answer

lines.text: Where was his son when they did take his eyes?
lines.plainText: Where was his son when they did take his eyes

lines.text: Come with my lady hither.
lines.plainText: Come with my lady hither

lines.text: He is not here.
lines.plainText: He is not here

lines.text: No, my good lord; I met him back again.
lines.plainText: No my good lord I met him back again

lines.text: Knows he the wickedness?
lines.plainText: Knows he the wickedness

lines.text: Ay, my good lord. 'Twas he inform'd against him;
lines.plainText: Ay my good lord 'Twas he inform'd against him

lines.text: And quit the house on purpose, that their punishment
lines.plainText: And quit the house on purpose that their punishment

lines.text: Might have the freer course.
lines.plainText: Might have the freer course

lines.text: Gloucester, I live
lines.plainText: Gloucester I live

lines.text: To thank thee for the love thou show'dst the King,
lines.plainText: To thank thee for the love thou show'dst the King

lines.text: And to revenge thine eyes. Come hither, friend,
lines.plainText: And to revenge thine eyes Come hither friend

lines.text: Tell me what more thou know'st.
lines.plainText: Tell me what more thou know'st
